accuracy.evidence: Checked for rainforest insects: leaf-cutter ants (Atta, Acromyrmex) cut leaves, chew them into mulch for a fungus garden and eat the fungus, not the leaves; big Atta nests hold millions of ants (Hölldobler and Wilson 2011; STRI). Insect abundance: Erwin 1982 found about 1,200 beetle species on 19 Luehea trees in Panama; Fittkau and Klinge 1973 put ants and termites at about a third of Amazon animal biomass. Blue morpho wings 12 to 20 cm across, structural blue on top, brown with eyespots beneath, hidden at rest (NHM London; Smithsonian). Hercules beetle males up to about 17 cm with horn, grubs in rotting wood. Orchid bees pollinate orchids and Brazil nut trees. The 15-animal count in the lab is labelled as a tally of what the child taps, not a census, and the adult text gives the real evidence.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets five documented slips: 'the big, famous animals are the most common' (prediction 1 and the tally where insects reach 11 against 4); 'leaf-cutter ants eat leaves' (prediction 2, the Feed them leaves button fails with a reason); 'a morpho is blue all over' (prediction 3, closed wings drawn brown with eyespots); 'all beetles are tiny' (prediction 4, the ruler puts a 17 cm beetle past the 13 cm hand); 'a spider is an insect' (the spider tile is counted as other with an 8-legs message, the visual sorter and practice p5). Leg-count confusion between insects and spiders is a common KS1 misconception noted in the Primary Science Teaching Trust and ASE guidance.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagraininsect is built on this topic's own content: a tap-to-count tally whose bars show insects outnumber other animals; a leaf-cutter scene where each leaf dragged to the nest grows the white fungus garden, then a feed choice; a blue morpho whose wings open blue and shut brown while a bird arrives, with a two-phase fly-then-hide rule; a centimetre ruler with a 13 cm hand outline where insects are drawn to scale. Gate: under 30% shingle overlap with every other flagship lab, including flagrainfood and flaganimrec.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers by doing: the tally bars grow as they count, so the insect majority is seen, not told; the fungus visibly grows with each leaf and feeding leaves fails, so the farming idea is found; opening wings with the bird present fails ('the bird can see that bright blue'), so hiding by showing the brown side is learned; the ruler shows which insects pass the hand line; jobs give a reason for wrong picks. Done messages confirm each idea.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'big ones, like jaguars and monkeys' (the tally), 'the leaves they cut' (feeding leaves fails), 'bright blue all over' (closed wings show brown with eyespots), 'beetles are always tiny' (the Hercules beetle crosses the hand line). Each step's done message reveals the locked-in prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven questions, each wrong option tagged to its own slip with its own message: big (big animals are easy to spot but fewer), leaf (ants feed the leaves to a fungus), roof (leaves are not a roof; they become fungus mulch), blue (only the top is blue), tiny (Hercules beetle 17 cm), spider (8 legs, a minibeast but not an insect), add (count on from 4: 5, 6, 7).

readability.evidence: Family lesson: kid text kept to short concrete sentences ('They are insects!', 'The ants eat the fungus.') within the learn/readability.py limit, adult text within its limit. Canvas labels are one to five words; key words (fungus, pollen, grub, morpho) are shown in pictures as they are named.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no filler phrases, under 12% overlap with any lesson). Each kid paragraph carries a fact (insects are most numerous and have 6 legs, ant farming, morpho colours, sizes and jobs); the adult paragraphs give curriculum links, numbers with sources, named mistakes and a lab summary.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: the 15 count tiles use 3 columns under 520 px with tiles at least 44 px high, tally bars sit below with readable labels; the leaf, nest and feed cards are large; the morpho fills half the width; the ruler cards sit in one row of four and the ruler labels stay inside the canvas; the three job cards stay readable. Young class gives 56 px buttons under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: Count the next animal (labelled with the animal), Carry a leaf home, Feed them leaves and Feed them fungus, Open and Shut the wings, Measure the ... for each insect, and a button per insect for each job with labels like 'Orchid bee: Carry pollen from flower to flower'. say() updates the canvas aria-label and a polite live region after every action; the walk gate's axe run is clean (WCAG 2.1 AA) in both themes on desktop and iPhone.
